quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Section 20 satisfies the preferred position in full. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables (20.1), and separately for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2) — matching limbs (a)-(d) of our model language. Standard procedure is present and balanced (20.4: prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-limited notice failure, and consent required for settlements admitting fault or not fully releasing the indemnified Party). The infringement remedy ladder in 20.5 (procure, modify/replace without materially reducing functionality, else terminate and refund on a straight-line three-year basis, with no right to terminate unaffected Services) exceeds the fallback. Notably, Vendor's IP indemnity in 20.1 carries none of the usual Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions, which is more favourable to us than either position. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 stays narrow as required — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with express carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or Vendor instructions. On the cap interaction, indemnification obligations are "Excluded Claims" under 21.3 and therefore fall outside the Section 21.1 liability cap entirely, which is better than the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap. (The narrow cap base in 21.1 — Fees under the first Order Form only — is a limitation-of-liability issue addressed under that rule and does not affect this indemnity, which is uncapped.) No redline warranted.

quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: The structure of Section 21 is otherwise strong: the cap is expressly mutual, indirect/consequential damages are mutually excluded (with restoration, replacement-service, notice and incident-response costs preserved as direct damages), Excluded Claims cover confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and the other Party's IP, and Customer's payment obligation is expressly not "damages". The cap quantum, however, fails the fallback: "Fees" is defined (1.5/1.6) as the Implementation Fee only — a one-time USD 12,000 charge under the first Order Form — so the twelve-month measure and the reference to "the first Order Form" reduce the cap to roughly USD 12,000 regardless of ongoing subscription and services spend. That is far below 6 months' fees and is an illusory cap in walk-away territory. Minimal fix: keep the sentence and mutual carve-out architecture, but measure the cap by all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor (preferred position). We did not amend the "Fees" definition itself to avoid disturbing the payment provisions.

Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position in full: six months of transition assistance at Order Form rates (more favourable to us than "then-current rates"), return of all Customer Data within thirty days of request in a complete, commonly used, documented machine-readable format with metadata, and secure deletion after confirmed return with written officer certification, subject only to a legally required retained copy that stays protected and use-restricted. Section 11.2 expressly bars Vendor from withholding Customer Data over a fee dispute, and Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) creates no competing withholding or immediate-deletion right. No redline required.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: Section 11.1–11.3 supplies all three preferred elements: up to six months of transition assistance (at expiring Order Form rates, better than then-current rates), return of all Customer Data within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and secure deletion with written officer certification thereafter. The only carve-outs (a legally required retained copy, kept protected and use-restricted; deletion from backups as they cycle) are standard and do not defeat the fallback, let alone approach walk-away territory (no data return / immediate deletion). Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or comment was proposed; the rendered text is unchanged and the deterministic check confirms a data return/transition clause is present. Rationale accurately reflects the cited paragraphs.

quote: 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.
rationale: Section 18 contains a Vendor insurance clause that meets the preferred position on every material term: commercial general liability of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate, professional errors and omissions of USD 2,000,000, cyber and privacy liability of USD 5,000,000 (appropriate given Vendor hosts Customer Data under Sections 15 and 17), and workers' compensation as required by law. Section 18.2 adds certificates of insurance on request, reputable insurers, primary coverage where customary, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities — all of which benefit us. quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
rationale: Section 19 meets the preferred position on every material term: 19.1 warrants Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel to industry standards, plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a ninety (90) day (i.e. 90 days / 3 months) Deliverable conformance warranty running from the later of delivery or acceptance, and warrants Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term (exceeding the 12-month software benchmark for a hosted product); 19.3 adds no intentionally introduced malicious code, Applicable Law compliance, no functionality diminishment and no contaminating open source; 19.4 supplies re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge escalating to termination and refund of Fees paid, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The 19.5 disclaimer is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty and the "AS IS" walk-away is not implicated. Section 6 acceptance does not truncate the period (it runs from the later of delivery or acceptance, and 6.2 adds an independent correction/termination/refund path); Section 3.1 reinforces the performance standard. The warranty period is therefore at least 90 days on substance. The only shortfall was drafting form: 19.2 spells the period out as "ninety days" with no numeral, which left the duration ambiguous on its face and failed the period check. The attached edit is a non-substantive clarification inserting "(90)" so the period reads "ninety (90) days"; it changes no commercial term, adds no obligation on Vendor beyond what 19.2 already provides, and can be dropped if Vendor prefers the words-only form.
